title: What do two Egyptian sums look like after every ten is swapped?
description: Two sums of Egyptian numerals are added by counting each symbol and swapping every ten, smallest first. In the first sum the swaps run all the way up to a finger, and each sum is checked by value.
teaching_notes: One idea: count each kind of symbol, then swap every ten for one of the next landmark, smallest first, even when a new landmark appears. Watch for students who leave ten lotuses without swapping them.

source: Figure it Out (adding with landmarks, question 1)
video_script.why: The child uses the count-and-swap method from the heels and strokes example on two sums where the swaps climb higher.
video_script.substitution: More kinds of symbol are added, and in the first sum the swaps reach a finger.
video_script.anchor: the book's two Egyptian additions, each with a row of symbols on either side of a plus sign
video_script.payoff_line: The first sum is one finger, one coil, one heel and five strokes.

final_answer.value: (i) 1 finger, 1 coil, 1 heel, 5 strokes, which is 10115 (ii) 1 lotus, 1 coil, 2 heels, 6 strokes, which is 1126
final_answer.spoken: the first sum is one finger, one coil, one heel and five strokes, and the second sum is one lotus, one coil, two heels and six strokes

hold_back: (i) 1 finger, 1 coil, 1 heel, 5 strokes, which is 10115 (ii) 1 lotus, 1 coil, 2 heels, 6 strokes, which is 1126
maths_rules: stroke 1, heel 10, coil 100, lotus 1000, finger 10000; ten of one make one of the next
(i) result 1 finger, 1 coil, 1 heel, 5 strokes = 10000 + 100 + 10 + 5 = 10115; check 9608 + 507 = 10115
(ii) result 1 lotus, 1 coil, 2 heels, 6 strokes = 1000 + 100 + 20 + 6 = 1126; check 1080 + 46 = 1126
video_script.design: One idea: swap tens upwards, even into a new landmark. The two sums stay on the board while the counts and swaps appear below them.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding Egyptian numerals.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>A stroke is one, a heel is ten, and a coil is one hundred. A lotus is one thousand, and a finger is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must add nine lotuses, six coils and eight strokes to five coils and seven strokes.
<bookmark mark='ask2'/>We must also add one lotus and eight heels to four heels and six strokes. Which symbols does the first sum have?

beats.on_screen: the questions stay on the board with the empty boxes

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ten of a symbol slide into one of the next symbol along the row stroke, heel, coil, lotus, finger

marks.gather: the same kinds of symbol are gathered together
marks.swap: ten of a symbol slide into one of the next symbol, smallest first

narration: <bookmark mark='gather'/>As in the example in your book, we count each kind of symbol together.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Then we swap every ten for one of the next symbol, starting from the smallest.

beats.on_screen: Given: (i) 9 lotuses, 6 coils, 8 strokes + 5 coils, 7 strokes; (ii) 1 lotus, 8 heels + 4 heels, 6 strokes
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, first, nine lotuses, six coils and eight strokes, plus five coils and seven strokes.
<bookmark mark='given2'/>Second, one lotus and eight heels, plus four heels and six strokes.

beats.on_screen: To find: both sums in Egyptian symbols

marks.find: the words both sums are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find both sums, written in Egyptian symbols.

marks.strokes: 8 + 7 = 15 is written and ten strokes slide into one heel

narration: <bookmark mark='strokes'/>Step one, take the first sum and start with the strokes. Eight plus seven is fifteen, which is one heel and five strokes.
<bookmark mark='heels'/>There were no heels before, so now there is one heel.

beats.on_screen: (i) coils: 6 + 5 = 11 = 1 lotus and 1 coil; lotuses: 9 + 1 = 10 = 1 finger

marks.coils: 6 + 5 = 11 is written and ten coils slide into one lotus
marks.lotus: the lotuses become 9 + 1 = 10, and ten lotuses slide into a finger

narration: <bookmark mark='coils'/>Step two, count the coils. Six plus five is eleven, which is one lotus and one coil.
<bookmark mark='lotus'/>The lotuses are now nine plus one, which is ten. Ten lotuses make one finger, and no lotus is left.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check the first sum by value. Nine thousand six hundred eight plus five hundred seven is ten thousand one hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Ten thousand plus a hundred plus ten plus five gives the same total.

beats.on_screen: (ii) strokes: 6; heels: 8 + 4 = 12 = 1 coil and 2 heels; coils: 1; lotuses: 1

marks.second: the strokes 6 are written for the second sum
marks.twelve: 8 + 4 = 12 is written and ten heels slide into one coil

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step four, take the second sum. The strokes are only six, so nothing is swapped there.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Heels come to eight plus four, which is twelve. That is one coil and two heels. The lotus stays as one.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the second sum by value. One thousand eighty plus forty six is one thousand one hundred twenty six.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>A thousand plus a hundred plus twenty plus six gives the same total.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (i) 1 finger, 1 coil, 1 heel, 5 strokes, which is 10115 (ii) 1 lotus, 1 coil, 2 heels, 6 strokes, which is 1126
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first sum is one finger, one coil, one heel and five strokes. It is ten thousand one hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The second sum is one lotus, one coil, two heels and six strokes. It is one thousand one hundred twenty six.
